subject: ldply NonlinearLS Predict, output of unequal length

messages.subject: ldply NonlinearLS Predict, output of unequal length
parts:
Yesterday, I was asked by a colleague to try and make some graphs with fitted non-linear models annotated with the equation and a measure of fit. I have managed to construct a series of models for the variable (Variety) being tested, but when I wanted to put them on the graph I came across this: 
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1376967/using-stat-function-and-facet-wrap-together-in-ggplot2-in-r

Essentially, it's saying that you can't supply stat_function with parameters that vary by facet panel, which was my hope (I even pulled all of the parameters into a dataframe to do so). Is this still the case?

The suggested solution was to create a dataframe with predicted values and plot them using geom_line().  

So I have my models in a list from dlply(). 

dput() of m.photo below...

require(plyr)

nls.photo<-dlply(m.photo, .(Variety), function(X) nls(Photosyn ~ a*(1-exp(-c*Light)), data=X, start=list(a=asym, c=inflec), trace=TRUE))

I then try and run ldply() using predict to get some values for geom_line to plot... 

grid <- with(m.photo, seq(min(Light), max(Light), length = 100))

ldply(nls.photo, function(df) predict(df, x=grid))
Error in list_to_dataframe(res, attr(.data, "split_labels")) : 
  Results do not have equal lengths

Sure enough the forth model's output is much shorter and I have no idea why...
